current_row.boundary_rationale: The scene turns to Jeremiah's own movement once the siege lifts, וְהָיָ֗ה בְּהֵֽעָלוֹת֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים מֵעַ֖ל יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹֽה (oshb:Jer.37.11, byte), matching “When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh’s army,” (web:Jer.37.11); a setumah marks this same verse in the inventory (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration), texture at the turn rather than its warrant. He is seized at Benjamin's gate on a charge of desertion and brought before the officials, matching “When he was in Benjamin’s gate, a captain of the guard was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You are defecting to the Chaldeans!”” (web:Jer.37.13); the officials strike him and hold him in Jonathan the scribe's house, matching “The princes were angry with Jeremiah, and struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe; for they had made that the prison.” (web:Jer.37.15). A petuchah closes the span at oshb:Jer.37.16 (single-witness WLC attestation, weak, tier-3 corroboration), כִּ֣י בָ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל בֵּ֥ית הַבּ֖וֹר וְאֶל הַֽחֲנֻ֑יוֹת וַיֵּֽשֶׁב שָׁ֥ם יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים (oshb:Jer.37.16, byte), where Jeremiah is reported to have remained many days.

All the remnant of Judah, who have gone into the land of Egypt to live there, will know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.” (web:Jer.44.28) The sign formula opens next, וְזֹאת לָכֶ֤ם הָאוֹת֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי פֹקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּ כִּי֩ ק֨וֹם יָק֧וּמוּ דְבָרַ֛י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְרָעָֽה (oshb:Jer.44.29, byte), matching “‘This will be the sign to you,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will punish you in this place, that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for evil.’” (web:Jer.44.29) a setumah closes oshb:Jer.44.29 (single-witness WLC evidence, ranked tier-3 weak per the Prophets addendum), disclosed as texture rather than as this span's own end. The sign itself, Pharaoh Hophra given over as Zedekiah was given to Nebuchadnezzar, closes the chapter, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹ֠תֵן אֶת פַּרְעֹ֨ה חָפְרַ֤ע מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבָ֔יו וּבְיַ֖ד מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשׁ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֜תִּי אֶת צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה בְּיַ֨ד נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל אֹיְב֖וֹ וּמְבַקֵּ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ (oshb:Jer.44.30, byte), matching “Yahweh says, ‘Behold, I will give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was his enemy and sought his life.’”” (web:Jer.44.30) a setumah closes oshb:Jer.44.30 (WLC alone carries it, ranked tier-3 weak under the Prophets-addendum ruling), closing this span's own end verse, together with the chapter. A differently-shaped header opens next, dated inside its own verse to Jehoiakim's fourth year and addressed to Baruch personally rather than to the Egypt community at large, הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל בָּר֖וּךְ בֶּֽן נֵֽרִיָּ֑ה בְּכָתְבוֹ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה עַל סֵ֨פֶר֙ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֧ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֛הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.45.1, byte), matching “The message that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,” (web:Jer.45.1) and this unit is bounded there.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A bare list of place names opens this unit, formally distinct from the direct-address scene just closed, וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט בָּ֖א אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֶל חֹל֥וֹן וְאֶל יַ֖הְצָה וְעַל מופעת מֵיפָֽעַת (oshb:Jer.48.21, byte), matching “Judgment has come on the plain country— on Holon, on Jahzah, on Mephaath,” (web:Jer.48.21) — judgment is declared once and then simply repeated over town after town rather than addressed to any of them directly; this verse carries a ketiv/qere pair, מופעת written against מֵיפָֽעַת read (single-witness). The list continues without any further verbal frame, וְעַל דִּיב֣וֹן וְעַל נְב֔וֹ וְעַל בֵּ֖ית דִּבְלָתָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.48.22, byte), matching “on Dibon, on Nebo, on Beth Diblathaim,” (web:Jer.48.22), וְעַ֧ל קִרְיָתַ֛יִם וְעַל בֵּ֥ית גָּמ֖וּל וְעַל בֵּ֥ית מְעֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.48.23, byte), matching “on Kiriathaim, on Beth Gamul, on Beth Meon,” (web:Jer.48.23), and וְעַל קְרִיּ֖וֹת וְעַל בָּצְרָ֑ה וְעַ֗ל כָּל עָרֵי֙ אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב הָרְחֹק֖וֹת וְהַקְּרֹבֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.48.24, byte), matching “on Kerioth, on Bozrah, and on all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.” (web:Jer.48.24), closing the roll with a note that the towns lie far or near. The unit closes on a summary in body-part imagery, נִגְדְּעָה֙ קֶ֣רֶן מוֹאָ֔ב וּזְרֹע֖וֹ נִשְׁבָּ֑רָה נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.25, byte), matching “The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,” says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.48.25), ending on neum-YHWH. A fresh imperative with a different figure — drunkenness rather than a broken horn — opens the next verse, הַשְׁכִּירֻ֕הוּ כִּ֥י עַל יְהוָ֖ה הִגְדִּ֑יל וְסָפַ֤ק מוֹאָב֙ בְּקִיא֔וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לִשְׂחֹ֖ק גַּם הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.48.26, byte), matching “Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against Yahweh. Moab will wallow in his vomit, and he also will be in derision.” (web:Jer.48.26), and this row closes before it: הַשְׁכִּירֻ֕הוּ, byte-attested at oshb:Jer.48.26, is a plural imperative with object suffix, the same onset device class that drives the seam at oshb:Jer.48.9, so the verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה closing oshb:Jer.48.25 corroborates the close that imperative onset already carries, rather than standing as an unsupported driver on its own.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row on into the drunkenness scene that follows on the strength of the neum-YHWH closing it was considered; that closure is only one of two independent grounds here, since the form itself also shifts cleanly — a bare town-list with no addressee gives way to a fresh imperative scene with its own figure at the very next verse.
